name: Courts and Law of the Elysian Concord
summary: Court structure, lay assessors, judicial appointment, the legal profession, access-to-justice indicators, criminal grading and floor, procedural rights, wrongful conviction, and civil law.

courts.name: Mediation House
courts.summary: One per Commune; free, multilingual, voluntary in outcome but compulsory in attendance before most civil filings.

courts.name: District Court
courts.summary: First instance for criminal and civil matters; one professional judge sitting with two lay assessors drawn by lot.

courts.name: Regional Court of Appeal
courts.summary: One per Region; appeal on fact and law before three professional judges.

courts.name: The Court of Review
courts.summary: Final appeal on questions of law and harmoniser of law across the Regions; 45 judges sitting in panels of five. Says what the law means, not what it may be.

courts.name: The Constitutional Court (jurisdiction in the court system)
courts.summary: Separate apex for constitutional questions; says what the law may be. Composition and appointment are canonized in gov.institutions.

layAssessors.rationale: A decision-maker who cannot be selected, promoted, or retained by anyone has nothing to trade.

appointmentFloors: appointment by a body independent of the regional executive
judiciary.removalRequires: an Audit Service finding plus two-thirds of the appointing body

legalProfession.prosecutionTest: evidence supports conviction AND prosecution serves a public purpose
legalProfession.pleaBargainingRationale: A system that trades a sentence for a plea prices the right to trial, and Charter right 16 does not permit rights to have prices.

bodies.name: The Public Legal Service
bodies.summary: 1.16 million publicly employed advocates providing free criminal representation to all and civil representation to 62% of households; organisationally independent of prosecutors, police, and government, and constitutionally funded so the body defending people from the state cannot be starved by it.

bodies.name: Regional Prosecution Services
bodies.summary: Independent of both police and the regional executive; must decline a charge unless the evidence supports conviction and prosecution serves a public purpose, and must publish reasons for declining cases involving death or serious injury.

standing: any group of 100,000 residents by petition, without personal injury
remedyOrder: declaration of incompatibility with a deadline
constitutionalReview.remedyRationale: The humility clause operating as remedial doctrine: prefer the outcome that leaves the most room to correct a mistake.

criminalLaw.harmPrinciple: Conduct is criminal only if it harms or endangers an identifiable interest of another person, the public, or the biosphere.
criminalLaw.capContested: After the Kessander Plague reconstruction, the maximum sentence for an offence that killed 340 million was 30 years. Two amendment attempts have failed after adverse Review Panel opinions. Unresolved.

offenceBands.name: Band 1 — Regulatory and minor
offenceBands.summary: Mediation House, restoration order, or fine.

offenceBands.name: Band 3 — Serious harm
offenceBands.summary: Supervision or custody up to 4 EY.

offenceBands.name: Band 5 — Gravest
offenceBands.summary: Killing, mass ecological destruction, biosecurity offences, atrocity. Custody 15-30 EY; no limitation period.

planetaryOffences.name: Offences against the Article 12 systems
planetaryOffences.summary: Including extraction of retained carbon for combustion.

criminalFloor.name: No retroactive offence or penalty
criminalFloor.summary: Conduct is criminal only if defined by law before it occurred.

criminalFloor.name: Mental element required for custody
criminalFloor.summary: Strict liability only for regulatory offences punishable by fine.

criminalFloor.name: Presumption of innocence
criminalFloor.summary: Burden on the prosecution throughout; the only permitted reversals concern retaliation against protected disclosers.

criminalFloor.name: No double jeopardy
criminalFloor.summary: Except reopening on new evidence in favour of the convicted person, which may be done at any time without limit.

criminalFloor.name: Proportionality
criminalFloor.summary: Between offence and sentence, reviewable on appeal.

proceduralRights.name: Counsel from first contact
proceduralRights.summary: Questioning before counsel arrives is inadmissible for any purpose.

proceduralRights.name: Complete custodial recording
proceduralRights.summary: Held by the Record Office, not by police; a gap is presumed adverse to the state.

proceduralRights.name: Production before a judge within 48 hours
proceduralRights.summary: No exception, including under emergency powers.

proceduralRights.name: Remand limits
proceduralRights.summary: Judicial authorisation renewed every 30 days; trial must begin within 90 days or the person is released.

proceduralRights.name: Exclusion of unlawfully obtained evidence
proceduralRights.summary: No good-faith exception; derivative evidence excluded unless an independent source is proved.

proceduralRights.name: Reasons and appeal as of right
proceduralRights.summary: Every verdict and sentence publishes reasons; one appeal as of right on fact and law.

wrongfulConviction.note: The 0.7% figure is published as a floor on the true rate, not a measurement of it. A system reporting no wrongful convictions is assumed to be failing to look.

civilLaw.contractComprehensibilityRequirement: Terms are unenforceable if not reasonably comprehensible to the party bound.
civilLaw.tortBasis: fault-based, with strict liability for ecological damage and inherently hazardous activity
civilLaw.stewardshipObligation: An owner may not degrade land's ecological function; the obligation runs with the land and binds successors.

knownWeaknesses.name: Mediation opacity
knownWeaknesses.summary: 71% of civil disputes resolve without published reasons or precedent; systematic unfairness inside Mediation Houses would be invisible to the case law.

knownWeaknesses.name: Settlement pressure on the weaker party
knownWeaknesses.summary: Compulsory attendance plus an eager mediator can produce settlements a court would not approve. Partially mitigated, not solved.

knownWeaknesses.name: Legal pluralism and forum shopping
knownWeaknesses.summary: Thirty-four codes produce genuine forum shopping in commercial and family matters.

knownWeaknesses.name: Assessor variance
knownWeaknesses.summary: Lay assessors vary and outcomes vary with them; the Concord publishes the variance rather than hiding it.

knownWeaknesses.name: Delay at the apex
knownWeaknesses.summary: A conflict between Regional appellate lines can persist for a decade before the Court of Review resolves it.

knownWeaknesses.name: The 30-year cap
knownWeaknesses.summary: Publicly contested for atrocity; twice sustained against public opinion by Review Panels. Genuinely unresolved.

knownWeaknesses.name: Ecological offences are hard to prosecute
knownWeaknesses.summary: Diffuse causation, long latency, and corporate structure make band 5 ecological convictions rare relative to the harm done.

knownWeaknesses.name: Wrongful convictions are under-detected
knownWeaknesses.summary: The 0.7% figure is a floor and known to be one.

knownWeaknesses.name: Procedural cost
knownWeaknesses.summary: No plea bargaining, full recording, and universal representation make criminal justice slow and expensive by design.

knownWeaknesses.name: Model-code gravity
knownWeaknesses.summary: Convergence by attraction is voluntary in form; a Region departing from the model code faces friction that looks a little like compulsion.
